text:
Marathon Petroleum's stock rose modestly today, continuing a strong rebound from a 6.76% dip earlier this month. The gain sits within a broader recovery: the stock has climbed roughly $42 (11%) over the past five trading days, driven by refining fundamentals that have tightened considerably. US refineries are running at 95.2% capacity — near maximum utilization — while diesel and heating oil inventories remain relatively lean at 103.33 million barrels; the news of heating oil prices up 59% year-over-year reflects genuine scarcity that refiners can monetize through higher margins.

However, there's a headwind worth noting: Russian crude production has rebounded to 8.73 million barrels per day as Gulf exports recovered, pushing global oil markets back into surplus according to the International Energy Agency. That shift away from supply tightness could eventually pressure refining margins, even as current inventory levels still favor the company.
